2610.08405.title: Learning from Failures: A Failure-Driven Prompt Refinement for LLM-Based Vulnerability Analysis
2610.08405.paper_summary: Large Language Models have emerged as promising tools for software vulnerability analysis, but their effectiveness depends heavily on prompt design. Existing research primarily compares prompting strategies using aggregate performance metrics, providing limited insight into why models fail or how prompts can be improved systematically. We propose Failure-Driven Prompt Refinement (FDPR), a methodology that analyzes recurring model failures to guide evidence-based prompt refinement. Using the Damn Vulnerable Java Application (DVJA), we identify recurring failure modes, including false positives, false negatives, unsupported reasoning, and CWE misclassification, and translate them into targeted prompt refinements. We then evaluate the resulting prompt on the Juliet Test Suite and perform cross-model validation to assess generalizability. The results show that failure-driven refinement improves the reliability of LLM-based vulnerability analysis while yielding reusable prompt design principles. More broadly, this work demonstrates that recurring model failures provide a principled foundation for prompt engineering, enabling the systematic development of more reliable LLM-based vulnerability analysis systems.
2610.08405.paper_summary_zh: 大型語言模型已成為軟體漏洞分析的有前景工具，但其效能在很大程度上依賴於提示設計。<lb/>現有研究主要比較提示策略，使用綜合性能指標，對模型失敗的原因或如何系統性改善提示提供了有限的見解。<lb/>我們提出了失敗驅動的提示精煉（FDPR），這是一種分析重複模型失敗以指導基於證據的提示精煉的方法論。<lb/>使用Damn Vulnerable Java Application (DVJA)，我們識別出重複的失敗模式，包括誤報、漏報、不支持的推理和CWE錯誤分類，並將其轉化為針對性的提示精煉。<lb/>然後，我們在Juliet測試套件上評估所得到的提示，並進行跨模型驗證以評估其可推廣性。<lb/>結果顯示，失敗驅動的精煉提高了基於LLM的漏洞分析的可靠性，同時產生了可重用的提示設計原則。<lb/>更廣泛地說，這項工作表明，重複的模型失敗為提示工程提供了一個原則性的基礎，使得更可靠的基於LLM的漏洞分析系統的系統性開發成為可能。
